body:
# Independent audit of the actual normal-dependent same-separator bridge

Audited source:
`candidate 9158d8d941246660`,
Sections 1--7. Result: **PASS**, with no repair identified.

This audit rederived the new realization, cover, continuation and common
allocation bridges. It did not merely invoke the final conditional dual.
The existing compact positive minimal-bad-base framework and the previously
proved energy/attainment theorems remain named inputs. Nothing here asserts
the existence of a bad body or proves OC.

## 1. Order of dependence and full-parameter source geometry

Scalar-penalized attainment and epsilon comparable to tau are proved before
the response dual. Each attained triple is a joint body/parameter minimum
at its fixed epsilon. Sampled polyhedrality and zero-plane exclusion then
give a finite-PL L positive on a neighborhood. Uniform physical-buffer
vanishing, own-source inballs, and shifted own-section properness are
geometric inputs established without the separator. This order is not
circular. In particular the source does not use the eventual scalar force
identity to manufacture its initial properness premise.

I reread the finite-hull supergradient construction in
`candidate c0fc791108fc8765`.
Its fixed-matrix support LP gives bounded slopes even at a boundary base;
marked own inballs and the optimal denominator floor give local Lipschitz
energy. The finite convex extension then yields the required full energy
supergradient. This avoids the false general assertion that arbitrary
concave functions have finite boundary supergradients.

Let N=d+1 and F=E^(1/d). Differentiating in the continuous mark gives
grad F=(N/d)F a_E. Therefore the full buffer's own supergradient is exactly

    g=f a_E + f c/(N L),

with c in the own superdifferential of L. A convex combination of the
active affine planes of finite-PL L extends THIS c to a full supergradient.
Combining it with the energy tangent proves the printed full tangent of
f. Thus the extra continuous L-gradient is retained; the old energy-only
alignment is not silently reused. The strict own concavity follows from
strict concavity of F and the strict increase of the positive geometric
mean in F. Boundary continuity uses the established energy theorem.

## 2. Finite actual cover, parity count and exact old contacts

I reread the local compact-tilt proof and source balance in Sections 4--5
of `candidate 86dd5366456916a8`.
It uses quantiles and convex source optimality, not a regular cap derivative.
The covariance-unit sphere is equally compact; the argument either works
directly with that sphere or follows by a fixed continuous affine change
making Sigma the identity. Near-active caps keep a proper own trace, so
the right quantile is locally strictly inverted after the trace-preserving
minimum-norm tilt clamp. Caratheodory gives at most d+1 actual mass-Q caps
with positive rho and sum rho u=epsilon g.

Here is a direct check of the face argument for the full L. Let
P_i=sum rho N, h_i=sum rho c, and let (alpha,g) be the full supergradient
of f at its source Y. At any other deepest mark Y_z, all Q-quantile
constraints give P_i.Y_z-h_i-epsilon f(Y_z)<=0. Concavity of f and the
continuous balance cancel the continuous displacement and give

    (sum rho a - epsilon alpha).(z-p)<=0.

Thus this corrected base normal supports conv(I). It vanishes on the
minimal face F_p through p. On that face the tangent inequality gives
psi_i=P_i.w-h_i-epsilon f(w)>=0 for EVERY actual point of the fiber.
At its deepest marks the reverse quantile inequality forces equality
and, because rho is positive, equality of every selected quantile.

Strict own concavity makes psi_i strictly convex on interior segments.
Two interior zeros are impossible. If a boundary zero and the known
interior zero existed, convexity and nonnegativity would force two
interior zeros along their segment. Hence there is exactly one zero
in each assigned sampled fiber and it is interior. This proves a finite
contact set without regularity or a differentiable source path.

Deepest marks form a convex depth region, so I is lattice-complete in
its hull. If witnesses in two different maximal minimal faces had the
same parity, their integer midpoint would be deepest. Its minimal face
contains both old minimal faces, contradicting maximality. The resulting
at-most-k(I) groups cover all deepest bases, and overlaps are retained.
No assertion that the cap normals sum to zero or cover an entire affine
continuous plane is inserted.

## 3. Signed normal-dependent fields really are compatible bodies

For a continuous globally finite Phi(u,w), convex in w for each unit u,
the constraint u.x+t Phi(u,z,x)<=h_Kz(u) defines a convex fiber. Uniform
lower linear bounds hold even when Phi is negative: on compact base and
normal sets, its values on a fixed continuous-coordinate ball are uniformly
bounded, so subgradients there are uniformly bounded and provide a common
affine lower bound. Testing u=x/|x| then bounds every new fiber for small t.
On that bounded region |Phi|<=A. This yields outer distance O(t), while
an inner homothety about the old inball gives positive interior and an
inner O(t) bound. No nonnegativity of Phi is used.

For every anchored relation, convexity in the FULL physical variables
gives

    u.sum lambda x_z + t Phi(u,q,sum lambda x_z)
       <=sum lambda[u.x_z+t Phi(u,z,x_z)]
       <=sum lambda h_Kz(u)<=h_Kq(u).

Thus the new sampled fibers satisfy exact anchored inclusion, and their
canonical hull has those exact fibers. The projection and complete
integer base are retained. This is not a later compatibility correction.

At a regular old radial endpoint x with normal n, the n constraint bounds
the outward radial change above by -t Phi(n,x)/(n.omega). A normal active
at the new endpoint gives the reverse bound using its nonnegative old
slack. Every subsequential active-normal limit supports x, so uniqueness
forces n. The inball bounds n.omega away from zero. These two bounds prove
the signed inward first speed Phi(n,x). The uniform O(t) radial bound
permits dominated convergence. Singular fiber-boundary points are surface
null; d=1 is the exact two-endpoint version.

Finite sums of fields remain in this cone, including signed affine
normal fields. A finite list is realized on one common small interval;
no common positive interval for an infinite list is required. Likewise
h+cL concave implies L+t h=(1-ct)L+t(h+cL) concave for small t. Positivity
persists on a common neighborhood and logarithmic normalization is a
positive scalar. The body, parameter, normal controls and signed scale
directions are simultaneously actual.

## 4. Independent normalization and contact-budget computation

With inward speed v put D=int v, s_L=M^-1 int log L v, and
H=M^-1 int h/L. Signed shell integration gives

    M_t=M-tD+o(t),
    log L_t=log L+t(h/L-H+s_L)+o(t),
    log f_t-log f
       =t[h/L-H+s_L-C_E/E+D/M]/N+o(t).

The first energy expansion is uniform on fixed own-interior neighborhoods:
the minimizing parameters have a common positive denominator floor and
converge uniformly to the old minimizers. This follows directly from the
signed shell/minimizer proof, reread in
`candidate d750a370b2e831ee`.
There is no derivative of grad L across a moving crease.

Since Sigma'=(D Sigma-Jmat)/M and Gamma(u_j)=1,

    (sum rho Gamma_t(u_j+t u'_j))'
       =D/(2M)-J_i/(2M)+sum rho grad Gamma(u_j).u'_j.

Combining this with epsilon'=epsilon s rederives the contact coefficient

    sum rho nu_j.Y_a - delta_a sum rho grad Gamma(u_j).u'_j
    +delta_a[C_E/(NE)+J_i/(2M)-(N+2)D/(2NM)
              -s_L/N-h(Y_a)/(NL_a)+H/N-s].

In particular every sign and the factor (N+2)/(2N) check. Joint boundary
continuity localizes the exact contact minimum to its finite old zero set;
the uniform interior expansion then gives the minimum of these linear
coefficients. No derivative of a newly chosen minimizing mark is needed.

## 5. Supporting caps and the actual common-quantile cover

For an outside supporting facet, radial clipping gives a cap GAIN
[(nu.w-r)/|u|-v]_+. It therefore appears negatively in the LOSS. Inside
support contributes its full-fiber body loss plus a nonnegative hinge.
Dropping only that hinge gives the printed concave lower response R^0.
The proper own coarea is positive, so R^0 is strictly increasing onto
the whole real line in r; all supporting allocations remain compact.
These facts hold for signed v, d=1 endpoints, and positive-area facets.

The exact scalar quantile equation and the contact minimum imply

    sum rho [N_j(t).w-epsilon(t)Gamma_t(u_j(t))f_t(w)
                                      -c_j(t,q_i(t))]>=0

throughout every assigned current fiber. One threshold is therefore at
least its q_i quantile and its captured mass is at most q_i. This is the
actual upper covering comparison. The old off-deepest-base gap persists
by compact upper semicontinuity, so simultaneous strict group improvement
would decrease the actual global objective.

For clarity, the conservative equalized loss is concave also without a
formula: its hypograph is the projection of the convex set
R_j^0(v,nu,r_j)>=ell, sum rho r_j=alpha. Taking the minimum over the
finitely many contact budgets preserves concavity. This validates the
response-cone separation, without differentiability of a selected cap.

## 6. Why ONE allocation works for all fields

Fix the finite cap groups and contact sets BEFORE choosing any tests.
For a finite test list, the outside-selector moment images are compact;
proper coareas are uniformly positive, so the equalized linear branch
forms form a compact set. If their convex hull failed to meet the polar
of the finite actual-direction cone, finite-dimensional separation would
produce a direction making EVERY branch/group improvement strictly
positive. That would contradict the actual cover comparison above.
Thus a convex mixture of genuine branch gradients exists.

The all-test compact space stores cap weights, contact weights and
WEIGHTED outside densities, not unstable quotients at zero weights.
All weights are nonnegative with total cap weight one; the coarea
relations bound the contact weights. Densities lie between zero and
their cap weights on fixed finite-measure old facets. Their weak-star
space is compact. Every fixed physical speed is bounded and measurable
and hence an L1 test of those densities. All moment, coarea and tested
inequality constraints are therefore closed. Any finite union of tests
was covered by the preceding actual finite-cone argument. The finite
intersection property yields ONE dual for all of them.

Both signs of every shared cap-normal control and logarithmic-scale
control are included in every finite list. They yield the stated
kappa-weighted section mean and the scalar coefficient M tau-Delta=0.
They do not force a section centroid at each individual contact. Inside
selectors retain the conservative convention; no independently chosen
inside/outside or parameter-only dual is substituted.

## 7. Checks, applicability and limitations

The following dependency verifiers were independently rerun:

* `supporting computation verify_nonregular_multicontact_log_flux_defect_transport.py`:
  813 exact aggregation/moment checks PASS;
* `supporting computation verify_log_buffer_scale_separator_defect_transport.py`:
  64 exact checks PASS;
* `supporting computation verify_supporting_cap_directional_inverses_slab_recovery.py`:
  197 exact checks PASS, including 168 actual clipped parallelograms.

The proof of the new bridges is the analytic argument above; these checks
are not used to infer them from finite examples.

Exact affine coordinate symmetries can be composed with the actual paths;
the source correctly avoids pretending their pullback of finite-PL L
has a uniform differentiable parameter jet. No new claim of admissibility
for arbitrary formal boundary arrays, all possible inside allocations,
or a derivative of the optimized depth is made.

This closes the previously conditional common-cone issue in Sections 7--8
of `candidate 7234d49b6c886f4b` at the
selected small logarithmic-scale minima of the stated framework. For the
ordinary limit, retain the outer normal in the joint boundary measure and
use the separately proved vanishing correction. A fixed continuous field
is bounded on the common compact normal/physical range, so its inequality
passes to that limit with the SAME weights/allocated selectors. It does
not create a finite limiting cap menu or a numerical Gamma bound.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
